H-OS-L1.name: Pebble
H-OS-L1.sphere: H-OS-L1 (Pebble, n=95, mean=7.15, std=1.78, confidence=strong) is the HEALING series leader by n and mean, with right-skewed distribution peaking at 8–9 (43 responses). Qualitative (n=29) shows 83% noticeable-or-better, settle ~5–10 min, activity includes driving/commuting (5), music liked/loved (19/29). AutoGluon predicts 6.859 for overstim — a 0.29 under-prediction, rare alignment. YouTube: 30 views, no retention. The strong consistency across high n, qualitative settle speed, and model agreement makes this the library's most validated descent protocol. Volume note: VOL001 only.
H-OS-L1.sphere_plain: Pebble is the most reliable protocol for overstimulation — most people feel clearly better, quickly, and love the music. It works well during commutes and busy moments.

H-OS-L2.name: Rainfall
H-OS-L2.sphere: H-OS-L2 (Rainfall, n=51, mean=6.92, std=1.73, confidence=strong) mirrors L1 shape shifted left by ~0.2, peak at 7–8. Qualitative (n=21) shows settle ~10 min, activity relaxing/listening, music opinion split (liked 10, neutral 6). The 'noticeable improvement' mode (10/21) vs 'significant' (3) suggests Rainfall groove yields reliable moderate relief rather than breakthrough. YouTube: 5 views. VOL001 only. Consistent performer for steady overstimulation descent.
H-OS-L2.sphere_plain: Rainfall reliably takes the edge off overwhelm with a soothing rhythm. The improvement is steady rather than dramatic, and the music is liked but not loved.

H-OS-L3.name: Glacier
H-OS-L3.sphere: H-OS-L3 (Glacier, n=47, mean=7.04, std=1.68, confidence=meaningful) has the tightest overstim distribution (std 1.68) with peak at 8–9. Qualitative (n=23) reports settle ~5–10 min, activity trying to sleep (8), music opinion liked (11) / neutral (5), rhythm very settling (10). The bedtime-use cluster in qualitative aligns with descent design. YouTube: 8 views. VOL001 only. Glacier appears optimized for sleep-transition overstimulation — consider routing tag.
H-OS-L3.sphere_plain: Glacier is especially good for winding down at bedtime when overstimulated. The rhythm is both calming and clear, and the music is well liked.

H-AX-L1.name: Meadow
H-AX-L1.sphere: H-AX-L1 (Meadow, n=67, mean=7.22, std=1.93, confidence=strong) shows the highest mean in the anxiety triad with a wide, right-skewed distribution peaking at scores 8–10. Qualitative data (n=23) indicates 87% noticeable-or-better improvement, settle time ~10 minutes, and strong rhythm approval (13/23 very settling). AutoGluon predicts 7.838 for anxiety zone — a 0.62 over-prediction suggesting the model expects even stronger descent entrainment than observed. YouTube signal is negligible (7 views, no retention data). The bimodal-like spread (mass at 7 and 9–10) warrants investigation into groove-style sensitivity across listener subgroups.
H-AX-L1.sphere_plain: Most people with anxiety felt a clear improvement with Meadow, especially within the first ten minutes. The rhythm feels very settling, though a few listeners didn't notice much change.

H-AX-L2.name: Cottage
H-AX-L2.sphere: H-AX-L2 (Cottage, n=48, mean=6.94, std=1.62, confidence=meaningful) delivers a tighter, left-shifted distribution vs L1 with peak at 7–8 and no scores above 9. Qualitative feedback (n=20) shows mixed change_rating (noticeable 6, moderate 6, slight 5) and bimodal settle time (5 min vs 20 min), suggesting context-dependent onset. Music opinion splits between liked (9) and neutral (5). Cross-volume comparison not available (VOL001 only). The narrower std but lower peak suggests this groove may trade peak efficacy for consistency — a candidate for adviser routing based on desired onset profile.
H-AX-L2.sphere_plain: Cottage helps with anxiety for many, but the effect is more moderate and takes longer to settle for some. The music is comfortable but not everyone loves it.

H-AX-L3.name: Valley
H-AX-L3.sphere: H-AX-L3 (Valley, n=36, mean=7.08, std=1.89, confidence=meaningful) sits between L1 and L2 with a secondary peak at 10 (5 responses) and a 'no effect' tail (2). Qualitative (n=20) reports 75% noticeable-or-better, settle ~10 min, rhythm very settling (10/20). Distribution [0,0,0,1,3,2,8,8,5,4,5] shows bimodal tendency at 7 and 10. YouTube: 4 views, no retention. The dual peaks at moderate and significant improvement suggest Valley groove may resonate strongly with a subset while under-serving others — warrants groove–subgroup mapping.
H-AX-L3.sphere_plain: Valley gives a noticeable lift for most anxious listeners, with a calming rhythm. A small group felt no effect, so it may not suit everyone equally.

H-CR-L1.name: Anchor
H-CR-L1.sphere: H-CR-L1 (Anchor, n=43, mean=6.35, std=1.70, confidence=meaningful) is the lowest-scoring crisis protocol with a left-weighted distribution [0,0,1,1,5,7,6,9,12,2,0] and pct_pos=53%. Qualitative (n=24) shows 79% noticeable-or-better but mixed listener types (self 11, client 7, support 5) and settle ~5–10 min. AutoGluon crisis prediction routes to H-CR-L2 (7.955), not L1 — model disfavors this groove for acute descent. The bimodal low-end (scores 4–5 mass) aligns with structural expectation for crisis descent but the AutoGluon delta suggests Anchor groove may not entrain rapidly enough for the most acute states.
H-CR-L1.sphere_plain: People in acute distress reported feeling better with Anchor, though the improvement tends to be moderate rather than dramatic. It helps people settle within 5–10 minutes.

H-CR-L2.name: Harbor
H-CR-L2.sphere: H-CR-L2 (Harbor, n=33, mean=6.52, std=1.70, confidence=meaningful) matches L3 mean with tighter low-end and pct_pos=55%. Qualitative (n=16) shows faster settle (5–10 min dominant), rhythm very settling (8/16), but music opinion split (neutral 6, loved 5). AutoGluon predicts 7.955 for crisis zone — largest positive delta in library (+1.43). This gap, combined with qualitative 'very settling' rhythm approval, signals that listeners who stay experience strong effect but early drop-off may depress observed mean. Development signal: test extended hold or slower descent entry to capture the disengaged tail.
H-CR-L2.sphere_plain: Harbor calms people in crisis quickly, with a very settling rhythm. Some listeners aren't sure about the music, but those who stay with it feel a strong effect.

H-CR-L3.name: Horizon
H-CR-L3.sphere: H-CR-L3 (Horizon, n=27, mean=6.52, std=1.91, confidence=meaningful) has the widest crisis spread with bimodal peaks at 7 (6) and 10 (3) and a 'no effect' tail. Qualitative (n=19) reports immediate settle (7/19) and mixed music opinion (liked 7, not liked 4). Listener types include working/studying (7) — unusual for crisis. The distribution suggests Horizon groove may work well for functional crisis (working through distress) but less for acute bedrest states. Cross-volume: VOL001 only. YouTube: 5 views, no retention.
H-CR-L3.sphere_plain: Horizon helps some in crisis right away, especially if they're working or studying through it. The rhythm is calming, but a few disliked the music.

H-SL-L1.name: Lantern
H-SL-L1.sphere: H-SL-L1 (Lantern, n=54, mean=7.19, std=1.86, confidence=strong) leads sleep protocols with right-skewed distribution peaking at 8–9. Qualitative (n=15) shows self-listeners dominant (13), settle ~5 min immediate (8), activity therapy/studying, music liked/loved (13). Rhythm very settling (4) / balanced (7). Cross-run drift notable (sim=0.530) — response pattern shifting as data grows. AutoGluon predicts 7.539 (Δ−0.35). YouTube: 4 views. The drift signal plus strong qualitative 'immediate settle' suggests Lantern groove may be gaining efficacy or attracting a changing listener mix.
H-SL-L1.sphere_plain: Lantern helps many people relax or fall asleep, often within five minutes. The rhythm feels very settling, and most listeners enjoy the music.

H-SL-L2.name: Hammock
H-SL-L2.sphere: H-SL-L2 (Hammock, n=45, mean=7.09, std=1.55, confidence=meaningful) has the lowest std in HEALING with peak at 7–8 and no scores below 4. Qualitative (n=15) shows client/patient listeners (6), settle ~10 min, activity studying/driving, music opinion neutral (6) / liked (5) — notably cooler music reception. The tight distribution but lukewarm music opinion suggests functional entrainment without aesthetic delight — a plausible maintenance groove. VOL001 only. YouTube: 5 views.
H-SL-L2.sphere_plain: Hammock works reliably for sleep and relaxation, though the music gets mixed reactions. People using it for therapy or studying find it helpful.

H-SL-L3.name: Midnight
H-SL-L3.sphere: H-SL-L3 (Midnight, n=28, mean=7.07, std=1.68, confidence=meaningful) peaks at 8 (7) with balanced spread. Qualitative (n=22) shows self (12), support (7), settle ~5–10 min, activity relaxing/care-giving, rhythm very settling (9) / balanced (7). Music opinion liked (8) / neutral (6). Cross-run drift notable (sim=0.611). YouTube: 3 views. VOL001 only. Midnight groove shows consistent sleep-onset profile with strong rhythm approval — candidate for caregiver routing.
H-SL-L3.sphere_plain: Midnight supports sleep onset with a balanced, calming rhythm. Caregivers and supporters also find it useful, and most like the music.

T-FC-L1.name: Compass
T-FC-L1.sphere: T-FC-L1 (Compass, n=41, mean=6.46, std=1.82, confidence=meaningful) is the lowest focus protocol with left-weighted distribution and notable scores at 3–4. Qualitative (n=23) shows settle ~5 min immediate, activity studying/relaxing, rhythm slightly busy (9) — busiest in focus triad. AutoGluon predicts focus zone winner as T-FC-L3 (7.728). The rhythm 'slightly busy' mode aligns with lower scores — groove may overstimulate for focus hold. Development signal: simplify rhythm density.
T-FC-L1.sphere_plain: Compass helps with focus for some, but the rhythm feels a bit busy for others. People studying or relaxing report moderate improvement.

T-FC-L2.name: Waypoint
T-FC-L2.sphere: T-FC-L2 (Waypoint, n=32, mean=7.19, std=1.60, confidence=meaningful) jumps +0.73 vs L1 with peak at 8–9. Qualitative (n=17) shows settle ~5–10 min, activity care-giving/therapy, music opinion neutral (6) / loved (5), rhythm balanced (8). The mean recovery with neutral music opinion suggests functional entrainment independent of aesthetic preference. Cross-run drift notable (sim=0.633). YouTube: 4 views.
T-FC-L2.sphere_plain: Waypoint gives a stronger focus boost with a balanced rhythm. The music is neutral for some, but the effect is reliable across different activities.

T-FC-L3.name: Summit
T-FC-L3.sphere: T-FC-L3 (Summit, n=35, mean=7.63, std=1.97, confidence=meaningful) is the library's overall mean leader with bimodal peaks at 7 (7) and 10 (10). Qualitative (n=29) shows support listeners (9), settle ~10 min (15), activity relaxing/chores, music loved (12) / liked (8), rhythm balanced (15). AutoGluon predicts 7.728 (Δ−0.10) — closest model alignment in library. Cross-run drift notable (sim=0.532). YouTube: 15 views. Summit combines peak efficacy, model agreement, and music delight — flagship hold-phase protocol.
T-FC-L3.sphere_plain: Summit is the clear leader for focus and clarity — most people feel significantly sharper, love the music, and find the rhythm perfectly balanced.

Cross-run drift: not flagged. YouTube: 2 views. The low peak (7 at score 6) and broad spread suggest Ember groove may not reliably entrain creative states — development signal for curve optimization.
T-CF-L1.sphere_plain: Ember gives mixed results for creative flow — some feel a clear lift, others only a slight change. The rhythm is comfortable but doesn't consistently spark creativity.

T-CF-L2.sphere: T-CF-L2 (Current, n=24, mean=6.79, std=1.41, confidence=meaningful) delivers the tightest creative flow distribution (std 1.41) with peak at 7–8. Aurora groove shows strong signal for creative flow hold-phase — warrants n≥50 confirmation.
T-CF-L3.sphere_plain: Aurora shows the strongest creative flow results so far — most feel a clear improvement with music they like. Still early data, but very promising.

T-MB-L1.sphere_plain: Stone offers consistent, calm maintenance support. The rhythm is very balanced, and it works well during therapy or before sleep.

T-MB-L2.sphere_plain: Axis gives mixed results for maintenance — some feel a clear improvement, others very little. It may work better for some listener types than others.

T-MB-L3.name: Orbit

T-MB-L3.sphere_plain: Orbit helps many settle quickly for maintenance, but a few don't settle at all. The music is liked, though early data means this picture could shift.

X-ME-L1.name: Breeze
X-ME-L1.sphere: X-ME-L1 (Breeze, n=39, mean=6.74, std=1.94, confidence=meaningful) is AutoGluon's top predicted protocol (8.230, Δ−1.49) but observed mean is moderate. The slow settle + prediction gap + music opinion split strongly signals early disengagement before ascent entrainment completes. Development signal: redesign initial ascent slope or add descent-on-ramp.
X-ME-L1.sphere_plain: Breeze has the highest predicted potential but takes the longest to settle (around 20 minutes). Many love the music, but the slow onset means some miss the benefit.

X-ME-L2.name: Sunrise
X-ME-L2.sphere: X-ME-L2 (Sunrise, n=25, mean=6.76, std=1.71, confidence=meaningful) shows bimodal settle (immediate vs 20 min) matching bimodal outcome potential. X-ME-L2.sphere_plain: Sunrise lifts mood and energy reliably for many, with a rhythm people love. It works both quickly and gradually, suiting different starting states.

X-ME-L3.name: Updraft
X-ME-L3.sphere: X-ME-L3 (Updraft, n=18, mean=6.28, std=1.74, confidence=developing) has lower mean than L1/L2 with peak at 7–8. Qualitative (n=18) shows settle ~5 min (8), activity studying/relaxing, music liked/loved (18), rhythm balanced (11). Despite highest music approval, outcome lags — suggests entrainment arc may not match mood/energy ascent expectation. YouTube: 4 views. The music delight / outcome gap warrants arc–expectation alignment review.
X-ME-L3.sphere_plain: Updraft has the most loved music in the mood series, but the lift isn't as strong as its siblings. The rhythm is comfortable but the ascent may be mismatched.

X-MD-L1.name: Footpath
X-MD-L1.sphere: X-MD-L1 (Footpath, n=22, mean=6.36, std=2.01, confidence=meaningful) has the widest motivation spread with mass at 4–6. Development signal: test slower ascent onset or extended initial hold.
X-MD-L1.sphere_plain: Footpath helps motivation for those who stay with it, but many may disengage before the full effect builds. The rhythm is comfortable and the music liked.

The rhythm delight + model preference + low n makes this a high-priority confirmation target.
X-MC-L2.sphere_plain: Starlight also clears the mind well with a deeply calming rhythm. Solo listeners studying or relaxing report strong effects, though data is still limited.

X-MC-L3.name: Cosmos
X-MC-L3.sphere: X-MC-L3 (Cosmos, n=10, mean=5.70, std=2.45, confidence=developing) is the library's lowest mean with bimodal [0,1,2,3] vs peers 6.75/6.81. Qualitative (n=17) shows self (7), client (7), change noticeable (9) / moderate (3) / slight (3), music liked (6) / neutral (5), rhythm very settling (6) / too busy (4). The distribution anomaly + 'too busy' rhythm + low n suggests Cosmos groove may mismatch mind clarity descent intent — candidate for redesign or retirement. YouTube: 8 views.
X-MC-L3.sphere_plain: Cosmos gives inconsistent results for mental clarity — some notice improvement, others don't. The rhythm feels too busy for a few listeners.

sphere_commentary.overview:
The three series deliver efficacy signals consistent with their design intent, with HEALING showing the most stable entrainment, THRIVING achieving the highest peak scores in cognitive protocols, and TRANSFORMING exhibiting expected variance from its ascending-arc architecture.
• HEALING protocols cluster at mean 7.0–7.2 with strong confidence tiers and the lowest cross-protocol variance
• THRIVING's Focus & Clarity L3 (Summit) reaches 7.63 mean (n=35), the library's highest observed score
• TRANSFORMING carries the widest spread (std 1.6–2.5) and largest AutoGluon–observed deltas, particularly in Motivation & Drive and Mood & Energy
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
Each series expresses its design signature in the outcome distribution.
• HEALING: consistent descent-phase regulation across anxiety, crisis, overstimulation, and sleep with strong confidence at n≥43
• THRIVING: hold-phase optimization yields the library's peak mean scores, notably in creative flow and focus protocols
• TRANSFORMING: ascent-phase protocols show high prediction–observation gaps (X-ME-L1 Δ−1.49, X-MD-L1 Δ−1.52), suggesting early disengagement before entrainment completes
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Three protocol clusters diverge from series-level patterns and warrant investigation.
• Crisis triad (H-CR-L1/L2/L3) means 6.35–6.52 with pct_pos 52–55% — structurally expected for acute states but AutoGluon predicts 7.955 for H-CR-L2, a 1.43-point delta
• X-MC-L3 (Cosmos, n=10) mean 5.70, std 2.45, bimodal [0,1,2,3] vs peers at 6.75/6.81 — possible groove mismatch or subgroup effect
• T-MB-L2 (Axis, n=22) std 2.03, widest in THRIVING, distribution [0,1,3] in lower bins — inconsistent with maintenance design intent
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Four high-convergence signals for protocol refinement.
• H-CR-L1 (n=43, mean=6.35): bimodal crisis response — investigate groove adaptation or adviser routing for acute descent entry
• X-MD-L1 (n=22, mean=6.36, AutoGluon 7.876): 1.52-point prediction gap — test extended hold or slower ascent to reduce early drop-off
• X-ME-L1 (n=39, mean=6.74, AutoGluon 8.230): top predicted protocol but moderate observed — slow settle (20 min mode) suggests arc–expectation mismatch
• T-FC-L1 (n=41, mean=6.46, std=1.83): widest creative flow distribution — optimize entrainment curve to capture more listeners
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Cross-run drift is pervasive across the library, indicating evolving response patterns or analytical instability as data accumulates.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: 24 of 30 protocols show notable drift (sim < 0.85); most extreme X-MD-L3 (0.507), H-SL-L1 (0.530), T-FC-L3 (0.532), X-ME-L2 (0.532)
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: Insufficient run history for cluster analysis
• Confidence note: Embedding data quantity remains low; drift signals should be treated as directional, not diagnostic

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: Most people with anxiety felt a clear improvement with Meadow, especially within the first ten minutes. The rhythm feels very settling, though a few listeners didn't notice much change.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: Cottage helps with anxiety for many, but the effect is more moderate and takes longer to settle for some. The music is comfortable but not everyone loves it.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: Valley gives a noticeable lift for most anxious listeners, with a calming rhythm. A small group felt no effect, so it may not suit everyone equally.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: People in acute distress reported feeling better with Anchor, though the improvement tends to be moderate rather than dramatic. It helps people settle within 5–10 minutes.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: Harbor calms people in crisis quickly, with a very settling rhythm. Some listeners aren't sure about the music, but those who stay with it feel a strong effect.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: Horizon helps some in crisis right away, especially if they're working or studying through it. The rhythm is calming, but a few disliked the music.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: Pebble is the most reliable protocol for overstimulation — most people feel clearly better, quickly, and love the music. It works well during commutes and busy moments.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Rainfall reliably takes the edge off overwhelm with a soothing rhythm. The improvement is steady rather than dramatic, and the music is liked but not loved.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Glacier is especially good for winding down at bedtime when overstimulated. The rhythm is both calming and clear, and the music is well liked.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: Lantern helps many people relax or fall asleep, often within five minutes. The rhythm feels very settling, and most listeners enjoy the music.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Hammock works reliably for sleep and relaxation, though the music gets mixed reactions. People using it for therapy or studying find it helpful.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Midnight supports sleep onset with a balanced, calming rhythm. Caregivers and supporters also find it useful, and most like the music.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: Ember gives mixed results for creative flow — some feel a clear lift, others only a slight change. The rhythm is comfortable but doesn't consistently spark creativity.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: Current provides steady, reliable support for creative focus. The music is enjoyable and the rhythm balanced, but it doesn't stand out as transformative.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: Aurora shows the strongest creative flow results so far — most feel a clear improvement with music they like. Still early data, but very promising.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: Compass helps with focus for some, but the rhythm feels a bit busy for others. People studying or relaxing report moderate improvement.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: Waypoint gives a stronger focus boost with a balanced rhythm. The music is neutral for some, but the effect is reliable across different activities.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: Summit is the clear leader for focus and clarity — most people feel significantly sharper, love the music, and find the rhythm perfectly balanced.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: Stone offers consistent, calm maintenance support. The rhythm is very balanced, and it works well during therapy or before sleep.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: Axis gives mixed results for maintenance — some feel a clear improvement, others very little. It may work better for some listener types than others.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Orbit helps many settle quickly for maintenance, but a few don't settle at all. The music is liked, though early data means this picture could shift.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Cavern clears the mind reliably with a very settling rhythm. People studying or supporting others find it helpful, and most love the music.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Starlight also clears the mind well with a deeply calming rhythm. Solo listeners studying or relaxing report strong effects, though data is still limited.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: Cosmos gives inconsistent results for mental clarity — some notice improvement, others don't. The rhythm feels too busy for a few listeners.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Footpath helps motivation for those who stay with it, but many may disengage before the full effect builds. The rhythm is comfortable and the music liked.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: Trail shows modest motivation scores but is loved by supporters helping others. It may work best when used indirectly for someone you're supporting.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: Switchback gives strong motivation boosts for some but not others — the picture is unclear with current data. Needs more listeners to interpret reliably.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: Breeze has the highest predicted potential but takes the longest to settle (around 20 minutes). Many love the music, but the slow onset means some miss the benefit.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Sunrise lifts mood and energy reliably for many, with a rhythm people love. It works both quickly and gradually, suiting different starting states.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Updraft has the most loved music in the mood series, but the lift isn't as strong as its siblings. The rhythm is comfortable but the ascent may be mismatched.
